events.description: O'Donnell's Foreign Policy Q&A with Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid ('Back to the future') in which he laid out what the Taliban would do.
O'Donnell and Hossaini witnessed Ismail Khan's militia beat two alleged Taliban to death and shoot the bodies in Herat.
Crowds in Kabul, Kandahar and other cities marched chanting Allahu Akbar (night after Herat rooftop chants); O'Donnell judged the war lost.
Kabul fell to the Taliban; O'Donnell left on the last civilian Turkish Airlines flight that day.
Taliban banned women from playing sport on return to power; women's cricket and football players fled to Australia and New Zealand.
O'Donnell detained in Kabul by the GDI ('a year under the Taliban'); taken to NDS HQ, forced to tweet a dictated apology twice and record a confession video; released same day and flew to Islamabad.
O'Donnell's driver Nasir held four days by the Taliban, beaten and sleep-deprived; car and phone confiscated.
Sirajuddin Haqqani travelled to the UAE and performed the Hajj in summer 2024, livestreaming it; required a UNSC travel-ban exemption.
New York Times profile portraying Sirajuddin Haqqani as a moderate hope for Afghanistan (interview conducted earlier in the year).
Taliban decree banning windows overlooking areas used by women ('ban on windows').

UK press (Telegraph, Times) urged England to boycott Afghanistan at the Champions Trophy; ECB refused unless boycott is united. O'Donnell: a boycott would be the first punishment the Taliban has faced since takeover.
O'Donnell launched 'Project Taliban' newsletter, first on Biden administration negotiations with Taliban/Haqqani leadership over five American hostages.
Massoud Hossaini won the Pulitzer Prize.

key_claims: The 'moderate Haqqani / Kabul vs fanatic Kandahar' framing is a deliberate campaign; Siraj and Jalaluddin rebuilt the Taliban, Hibatullah owes his position to Siraj, and all factions share the same ideology.
The Taliban is 'an extremely wealthy, clever mafia' trafficking drugs (expanding poppy/heroin and moving into meth), guns, people and antiquities, and has faced no punishment in 3.5 years.
Taliban links with al-Qaeda, Hamas, Hezbollah, the Iranian regime, the Houthis and Haqqani-IS links are denied by officials to the detriment of policy.

Western governments, military and diplomats 'gaslit' the public with 'Taliban 2.0' talk in 2021 while Afghans and reporters saw the collapse coming; the drawdown to 2,500 troops under Trump made withdrawal inevitable under Biden.
The GDI detention and forced confession of O'Donnell in 2022 showed the Taliban's true face and backfired by giving her a global platform.
Aid cash flows through Taliban-controlled NGOs; a Trump administration with Taliban-sceptic veterans and Rubio might audit it or harden policy.
A cricket boycott would be the first real sanction on the Taliban; the team is a Pashtun, Taliban-aligned prestige asset.
